title: aFRR, Automatic Frequency Restoration Reserves, Capacity Market
description: Energinet makes daily procurement of automatic frequency restoration reserves (aFRR) on an hourly capacity market. This site provides market-related information for the balancing capacity market. Here, you can find details on requested demand, procured volumes, and reserve prices across different directions and price areas per hour.
comment:
**Note:** The demand and procured volume may not match exactly. Some of the demand can be covered by other TSOs and likewise, the procured volume may help meet other TSOs’ needs. This is managed by the platform algorithm in the Nordic aFRR capacity market. 

For further information, please see: 
* [Nordic aFRR capacity market](https://nordicbalancingmodel.net/roadmap-and-projects/nordic-afrr-capacity-market)
* [Balancering og systemydelser](https://energinet.dk/el/balancering-og-systemydelser/)
* [Balancing and Ancillary Services](https://en.energinet.dk/electricity/balancing-and-ancillary-services/)

As of 2024-10-02, a new capacity market for aFRR DK1 has been introduced, and data has been added to the dataset. "Nordic" has been removed from the the dataset title.

The Upward demand and Downward demand columns contain values starting on 2025-08-21.

---
**API Request Frequency** \
To get the data for tomorrow, calling the API with a dynamic timestamp such as [start=StartOfDay%2BP1D](https://api.energidataservice.dk/dataset/AfrrReservesNordic?start=StartOfDay%2BP1D) is a good approach. Making a request every five minutes or so between 8:00 and 9:30 CET is sufficient to ensure getting the latest data.
author: Energinet

columns.description: A date and time shown in _UTC time zone_. It is the "from" timestamp for the period in which the values are valid. The dataset resolution sets the length of the interval.
columns.comment:
Please note that the _format_ shown in the example applies to data downloaded as JSON or fetched through the API.
The format is slightly different when it is shown on screen or downloaded manually as CSV or XLSX. This is mainly due to readability and consideration for Excel users.

**In preview (in the GUI)** all timestamps are shown as (display convention)
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mmZ
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:00Z. 
That is without the seconds. The Z will remind viewers that this is UTC.

In **download (CSV and XLSX)** the date time are exported as
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:00.
That is without the “T” and the “Z” and the seconds. Excel will recognize it as date-time. The user must remember the convention about time zones.

In **download (JSON and API)** the datetime is exported as
YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss
e.g. 2017-07-14T08:00:00.
That is without the "Z".
